title: Servo on Timer1: 16 MHz clock, prescaler 8. How many ticks is the 1.5 ms pulse (the OCR1A value)?
explain: Timer clock = 16 MHz / 8 = 2 MHz, so 2 ticks per microsecond. 1500 us * 2 = 3000 ticks. The 20 ms period is 40000 ticks (ICR1). Check the prescaler first: the same pulse is 24000 ticks with prescaler 1.

title: Servo angle to pulse width with Arduino map(), integer math. What does this print?
explain: Integer division truncates. (100 - 0) * (2000 - 1000) = 100000. 100000 / 180 = 555 (the .55 is lost). Then + 1000 gives 1555. map() never rounds. For a servo this error is tiny, but remember it for sensor values.

title: 9 V battery, R1 = 10 kΩ on top, R2 = 4.7 kΩ to GND. The divider output goes to a 10-bit ADC with a 5 V reference. What does this print?
explain: Vout = 9 V * 4.7k / 14.7k = 2.88 V. ADC = 2.88 / 5 * 1023 = 588.7, and the cast to int cuts it to 588. The divider keeps the pin below 5 V. Without it, 9 V on the pin would destroy the input.

title: TMP36 reading, 10-bit ADC at 5 V. Integer math with long. What does this print?
explain: mv = 160 * 5000 / 1023 = 782 (782.01 cut). TMP36 gives 500 mV at 0 C and 10 mV per C. t_x10 = 782 - 500 = 282, so 28.2 C. Keep the value times 10 as an integer, and split it only when you print. Beware of negative values: see the -0.5 case.

title: One 330 Ω resistor in series with two 330 Ω resistors in parallel. What is the total resistance?
explain: Two equal resistors in parallel give half: 330 / 2 = 165 Ω. Add the series resistor: 330 + 165 = 495 Ω. Parallel always gives less than the smallest part. Series always adds.

title: Cortex-M reset. What does the CPU read from the first two words of the vector table?
options: Word 0 = initial stack pointer (MSP), word 1 = address of Reset_Handler
Word 0 = address of Reset_Handler, word 1 = initial stack pointer
Word 0 = address of main, word 1 = address of HardFault_Handler
Both words are reserved and must be zero
explain: On reset the hardware loads MSP from word 0 and PC from word 1. That is why your linker script must put .isr_vector first, and why _estack is the first entry. The Reset_Handler address has bit 0 set (Thumb), so the value is odd.

title: int counter = 5; is a global. Where is the value 5 stored in the firmware image, and who puts it in RAM?
options: In flash (load address of .data). Reset_Handler copies it to RAM before main()
In RAM. The programmer writes it there with the flash
Nowhere. The compiler sets it when counter is first used
In flash only. The CPU reads counter directly from flash
explain: .data has two addresses. LMA: where the initial values sit in flash. VMA: where the variable lives in RAM. The startup code copies LMA to VMA. If you skip the copy, counter holds random RAM content after reset.
from: Boot from reset to main() · .data copy

title: The .data copy loop works with uint32_t pointers. _edata is 0x20000006 (not aligned to 4). What goes wrong?
options: The last word is written fully: 2 bytes after _edata are overwritten
The last 2 bytes are not copied
The loop never ends
Nothing, a Cortex-M handles it
explain: The loop runs while (dst < &_edata). At 0x20000004 it is still true, so it writes 4 bytes up to 0x20000007. The 2 bytes after _edata belong to the next variable. ALIGN(4) before _edata makes the section size a multiple of 4, so the word copy ends exactly.
from: Boot · ALIGN(4) in the linker script

title: Arduino Uno, lesson on interrupts. Which pins can you use with attachInterrupt()?
options: Pins 2 and 3
Pins 0 and 1
Pins 8 and 9
Any digital pin
explain: The Uno (ATmega328P) has two external interrupt pins: INT0 on pin 2 and INT1 on pin 3. Use digitalPinToInterrupt(pin) in the call. Other pins need pin change interrupts, which are a different mechanism with shared handlers.

title: Button ISR sets a flag. With optimization on, waitForPress() never returns. Tap the bug.
explain: The compiler does not know the ISR changes pressed. In the wait loop it reads the flag once and makes an endless loop. Declare it volatile. Remember: volatile fixes the re-read only. It does not make wider types atomic.
